why:
The other half of the §12.3 pair, isolated: here the only possible cause of failure is the literal PRICE. This case was born out of a proof that did not exist — until 31/08 the price appeared only in the `fail/` of the main case, next to a sentence, and since a single finding already becomes "reprovou" the sentence carried the side alone. Measured result: erasing the whole price detection (`if (preco)` → `if (false && preco)`) left the 51 proofs green. With this case, that mutation DIVERGES. The `fail/` is the `pass/` with ONE line planted, `R$ 4.900,00`, and the printed reason has a single finding: `app/pagina.tsx: price "R$ 4.900,00"`. Neither side has a single sentence the rule can see — the texts either live in ``, which is not in `PROSA`, or are pure interpolation (`

{conteudo.titulo}

`). If the sentence detection is switched off, this case stays green: it does not measure sentence, and that is why it measures price. The `pass/` exists to lock the DIGIT guard, and without its specimen the test would not exist: `R$ {formatarPreco(conteudo.precoEmCentavos)}` is a currency sign with NO digit, which is the RIGHT FORM — the symbol is code, the value comes from `conteudo/inicio.json` in cents and `app/lib/preco.ts` only writes the punctuation. Erasing the digit requirement from the pattern (`/R\$\s?\d[\d.,]*/` → `/R\$/`) paints this side red. Without that `R$` on the side that PASSES, loosening the pattern would cost nothing and the guard would be decorative — it was one of the nine mutations that survived in this rule in the 31/08 audit. Both sides are the same tree — same `conteudo/inicio.json` with `precoEmCentavos`, same formatter, same component. The only difference is the planted literal.
